info.title: Oremi Isinmi Agent Documentation
info.description:
**Oremi Isinmi Agent** is a powerful and user-friendly API for retrieving weather
forecasts, air quality data, pollen levels, geographical location data, and
server-related information. Built with FastAPI and designed to run in a Docker
container, Oremi Isinmi Agent provides developers with easy access to accurate
weather and geocoding data.

![Oremi Isinmi Agent Logo](logo.jpg)

## Features

- Alarm scheduling with custom labels and recurrence
- Flexible timers with countdown and cancellation support
- Persistent reminders with optional recurrence
- Calendar event creation and management
- Natural language understanding via Ollama (LLaMA3.2)
- Built with a focus on performance and security
- Easily deployable using the [`demsking/oremi-isinmi-agent`](https://hub.docker.com/r/demsking/oremi-isinmi-agent)
  Docker image.

## Deployment

### Docker Image

The [`demsking/oremi-isinmi-agent`](https://hub.docker.com/r/demsking/oremi-isinmi-agent)
Docker image is officially available on Docker Hub, supporting both
`linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` platforms. The image is configured to expose
port `7337`, which serves the API and documentation endpoints.

The local documentation can be accessed at `http://localhost:7337/docs` for easy
reference on available endpoints and usage instructions.

### Deploy with Docker

Use the official Docker image [`demsking/oremi-isinmi-agent`](https://hub.docker.com/r/demsking/oremi-isinmi-agent)
to run Oremi Isinmi Agent:

```sh
docker run -d --env-file <path_to_env_file> -p 7337:7337 demsking/oremi-isinmi-agent
```

Replace `<path_to_env_file>` with the path to your
[environment variables](#description/environment-variables) file containing the
necessary configurations.

### Deploy with Docker Compose

Create a `compose.yml` file:

```yaml
services:
  agent:
    image: demsking/oremi-isinmi-agent
    depends_on:
      - ollama
    volumes:
      - ~/.config/oremi-isinmi-agent:/var/cache/oremi-isinmi-agent
    environment:
      OLLAMA_BASEURL: http://ollama:11434

  ollama:
    image: ollama/ollama
    restart: always
    runtime: nvidia
    volumes:
      - ~/.ollama:/root/.ollama
```

Run the container using `docker compose`:

```sh
docker compose up -d
```

## Environment Variables

When configuring **Oremi Isinmi Agent**, several environment variables are used to
control its behavior and connect with external services. Below is a breakdown
of these variables, grouped by their purpose.

### HTTP Configuration

- **HOST**: The host address on which the application will listen. Default is `"127.0.0.1"`.
- **PORT**: The port number on which the application will listen. Default is `7337`.
- **USER_AGENT**: User agent string for HTTP requests. This string identifies
  the application and its version in HTTP requests. Default is
  `"<APP_NAME>/<APP_VERSION>"`.

### Caching Configuration

These variables control HTTP request behavior and caching settings.

- **CACHE_DIR**:
  The directory in which to store cached data. Defaults to `'/usr/local/cache'`.

### Ollama Configuration

- **OLLAMA_BASEURL**: Base URL of the Ollama API. Required for communication with Ollama services.
- **OLLAMA_MODEL**: Model name to use for Ollama services. Default is `"llama3.2"`.

### API and Logging Configuration

These variables control the API root path, logging behavior, and server settings.

- **ROOT_PATH**:
  Defines the base URL path for all API routes. Defaults to `'/'`.

- **LOG_FILE**:
  Path to the log file for storing application logs. Empty defaults to console.

- **LOG_LEVEL**:
  Controls the verbosity of logs. Options: `'DEBUG'`, `'INFO'`, `'WARNING'`,
  `'ERROR'`, `'CRITICAL'`. Defaults to `'INFO'`.

### Performance Configuration

Settings that control the server's performance.

- **WORKERS**:
  The number of worker processes for handling requests. Defaults to the
  number of CPU cores on the system.

post.description:
Loads the model for a specific language.

This endpoint is used to load the necessary model for a given language.
If the model is not available, an error message is returned.

parameters.name: language

schema.description: The language for which the model should be loaded.
schema.title: Language

parameters.description: The language for which the model should be loaded.

post.description:
Creates a schedule based on natural language input. The input text is
processed to extract scheduling details, which are then used to create
a schedule. A webhook URL is required to notify when the schedule
triggers. Optionally, a payload can be sent with the webhook.

This endpoint is useful for users who prefer to describe their schedule
in plain language instead of providing structured data.

schema.description: A natural language request to create a schedule.

examples.text: Set a reminder for a meeting at 10 AM tomorrow.

example.input: Set a reminder for a meeting at 10 AM tomorrow.
example.message: Reminder created for meeting with John.

content.title: Missing required information to create the schedule

example.message: You need to specify when you want to be reminded.

post.description:
Creates a new schedule using structured data. The schedule can be a
one-time event or a recurring event. For timers, the trigger time is
calculated based on the provided duration. The schedule is stored and
added to the scheduler for execution.

This endpoint is ideal for users who have precise scheduling details
and want to create a schedule programmatically.

schema.description: Details of the schedule to create.
schema.title: Schedule

get.description:
Retrieves a list of all active schedules. Users can filter the results
by schedule type or choose to only include schedules that are still
active. The schedules are sorted by their scheduled time.

This endpoint helps users view and manage their existing schedules.

parameters.name: type

schema.description: Filter schedules by type (e.g., alarm, timer).
schema.title: Type

parameters.description: Filter schedules by type (e.g., alarm, timer).

parameters.name: active_only

schema.description: If true, only return schedules that are still active.
schema.title: Active Only

parameters.description: If true, only return schedules that are still active.

delete.description:
Cancels a specific schedule by its unique ID. If the schedule is found,
it is removed from the scheduler and the active schedules list. If the
schedule does not exist, a 404 error is returned.

This endpoint is useful for users who want to stop a schedule from
triggering in the future.

parameters.name: schedule_id

schema.description: The unique ID of the schedule to cancel.
schema.title: Schedule Id

parameters.description: The unique ID of the schedule to cancel.

post.description:
Immediately triggers a specific schedule by its unique ID. The schedule
is executed in the background, allowing users to test or manually
trigger schedules without waiting for their scheduled time.

This endpoint is helpful for debugging or testing purposes.

parameters.name: schedule_id

schema.description: The unique ID of the schedule to trigger immediately.
schema.title: Schedule Id

parameters.description: The unique ID of the schedule to trigger immediately.

tags.name: Agents Endpoints
tags.description: Endpoints for managing schedules and triggering events. These endpoints allow users to create, list, cancel, and trigger schedules. They support both natural language input and structured data for creating schedules, providing flexibility for different use cases.

tags.name: Server Endpoints
tags.description: Endpoints for retrieving server-related metadata, such as the server's name and version. These endpoints help clients identify the server they are interacting with and ensure compatibility with the API.
